newsitem.title: CHINA: Rival Koreas reach pact on food aid for North.
newsitem.headline: Rival Koreas reach pact on food aid for North.

text.p: Red cross officials from rival North and South Korea on Monday signed an agreement under which Seoul will supply 50,000 tonnes of food aid by the end of July to its hungry Stalinist neighbour.
South Korean officials attending a signing ceremony hailed the accord as a boost to momentum in the development of North-Suth ties.
The accord, reached after three days of often difficult talks in the Chinese capital, calls for various land and sea routes to be used to deliver food to the famine-threatened North.
South Korean officials told reporters they were disappointed that Panmunjom, the town that straddles the heavily fortified border, would not be one of the routes.
They also said North Korea had agreed to accept donors' names on Red Cross packages.
